The raw retail bytes are a1 fc 8b 5c 00 c3 with nop padding after the ret; the candidate body at 0x0041F7F0 is a1 ec 1b 5e 00 c3, the same one-block load-and-return.

checks.name: argument_mapping
checks.rationale: The retail function takes no arguments and never reads the stack; the candidate AppContext_GetIsActive() also takes none and reads only the flag. The typed runtime contract therefore records no_arguments true, and the reviewed input observables are pre-call state (the flag value and the paired setter relation), not ABI parameters.

checks.name: constants_and_scaling
checks.rationale: There is no arithmetic, scaling or literal constant. The function is a pure 4-byte load of the flag dword and returns it unchanged; the observed values in the paired capture are 1 at the reviewed startup load and 1 as the final flag value, matching the paired setter store of 1.

checks.name: memory_layout_and_access
checks.rationale: The only memory access is the absolute 4-byte load from 0x005C8BFC at 0x0048F171 (a1 fc 8b 5c 00). That is the same dword the paired setter 0x0048F140 stores sign_extend_8(argument[7:0]) into at 0x0048F147, it lies in the zero-filled tail of .data, and the retail .text contains exactly two references to that VA: the store and this load. The candidate loads its equivalent global AppContext_IsActive (0x005E1BEC) with the same absolute addressing mode.

checks.name: calls_and_side_effects
checks.rationale: The function has no callees, no branches and no writes: EAX is loaded from the flag and returned, so the only observable effect is the read. The paired capture confirms flag_unchanged_during_call true and getter_wrote_nothing true on both sides. The reviewed invocation is the frame-loop call at 0x0048F812 (retail) and 0x00482D4F (candidate); the display window handler calls the same native on WM_ACTIVATE and those invocations are out of the paired scope.

checks.name: return_and_error_paths
checks.rationale: EAX receives the dword and is returned unchanged; there is no branch, no error path and no fallback value. The compared relation is return == flag at entry and return == the dword the paired setter wrote, which the runtime record confirms as return_equals_flag_before true and return_equals_setter_stored true.

checks.name: floating_point_semantics
checks.rationale: The function only loads and returns a 32-bit integer flag; it contains no x87, SSE or other floating-point instruction and no floating-point state is read or written. The candidate implementation likewise performs only an integer load.
